cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A first Class C instructional permit requires the secure-identity.
cards.back: A first Class C instructional permit requires the secure-identity documentation standards if the applicant has not already met them.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The Class C instructional-permit application.
cards.back: The Class C instructional-permit application is available beginning at age fifteen.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A permit applicant must establish identity, citizenship or lawful presence, and Georgia.
cards.back: A permit applicant must establish identity, citizenship or lawful presence, and Georgia residence, and must know the Social Security number or document ineligibility for one.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: An applicant younger than eighteen must provide school-enrollment evidence and obtain.
cards.back: An applicant younger than eighteen must provide school-enrollment evidence and obtain a parent, guardian or responsible adult's signature consenting to the permit.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The adult who signs a minor's permit application can revoke.
cards.back: The adult who signs a minor's permit application can revoke that permit for any reason before the holder turns eighteen.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Obtaining the instructional permit requires both a vision screening.
cards.back: Obtaining the instructional permit requires both a vision screening and the knowledge examination covering signs and driving rules.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The handbook lists a ten-dollar testing charge payable before testing, with no.
cards.back: The handbook lists a ten-dollar testing charge payable before testing, with no refund for a failed component and a new payment for each attempt.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A CP holder may drive a Class C vehicle only with a.
cards.back: A CP holder may drive a Class C vehicle only with a Class C licensed supervisor aged at least twenty-one, seated alongside the learner and fit and capable of controlling the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A Class D application ordinarily becomes possible at age sixteen after holding.
cards.back: A Class D application ordinarily becomes possible at age sixteen after holding a valid instructional permit for at least one year and one day.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A Class D applicant needs a road-test appointment and must surrender.
cards.back: A Class D applicant needs a road-test appointment and must surrender the CP or affirm on the application that surrender is impossible.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: For Class D, the applicant must document school enrollment and.
cards.back: For Class D, the applicant must document school enrollment and alcohol-and-drug-awareness education, obtain adult consent, and pass the road driving test.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The adult who consents to the minor's Class D.
cards.back: The adult who consents to the minor's Class D application may revoke that license before the driver turns eighteen.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: At age sixteen or seventeen, Class D requires.
cards.back: At age sixteen or seventeen, Class D requires both DDS-approved driver education and the alcohol-and-drug-awareness program.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The approved driver-education course includes thirty classroom hours or an equivalent online.
cards.back: The approved driver-education course includes thirty classroom hours or an equivalent online course, together with six hours of certified on-road instruction or completion of the DDS parent-teen guide.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The Class D education requirement also includes at least forty hours of.
cards.back: The Class D education requirement also includes at least forty hours of other driving experience, with at least six hours at night. A DDS affidavit signed at road testing certifies completion.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: When a certified instructor provides the on-road driver-education component, a.
cards.back: When a certified instructor provides the on-road driver-education component, a separate document confirming that component is required at the road test.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Without the required driver education, a teen cannot obtain Class.
cards.back: Without the required driver education, a teen cannot obtain Class D. The awareness program is available through many schools and online.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A teen whose parent is serving on active United States military duty.
cards.back: A teen whose parent is serving on active United States military duty may use an out-of-state driver-education certificate if it falls within nine months of the teen's sixteenth birthday.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment is exempt from the usual.
cards.back: A seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment is exempt from the usual one-year-and-one-day learner-permit holding period; the handbook says this applicant receives Class C.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A Class D holder is prohibited from driving from midnight until.
cards.back: A Class D holder is prohibited from driving from midnight until five a.m.; the handbook states that this restriction has no exceptions.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: During the first six months of Class D, passengers are restricted to.
cards.back: During the first six months of Class D, passengers are restricted to immediate family, including parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and anyone living at the driver's residence.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: In the second six months of Class D, the vehicle may carry.
cards.back: In the second six months of Class D, the vehicle may carry at most one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the driver's immediate family.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: After the first twelve months of Class D, at most three.
cards.back: After the first twelve months of Class D, at most three passengers younger than twenty-one may be outside the driver's immediate family.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Before seeking Class C, a Class D holder must have no conviction.
cards.back: Before seeking Class C, a Class D holder must have no conviction during the preceding twelve months for a major traffic offense that mandates license suspension.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A first Class C license requires the REAL ID.
cards.back: A first Class C license requires the REAL ID documentation standards if the applicant has not already satisfied them.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: At age eighteen, a Class D holder may seek Class C after.
cards.back: At age eighteen, a Class D holder may seek Class C after holding a valid Class D until that age or for one year and one day, with no major-traffic-violation conviction during the preceding twelve months.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A qualified United States citizen exchanging Class D for Class C must.
cards.back: A qualified United States citizen exchanging Class D for Class C must surrender the earlier credential or affirm inability to do so; the handbook requires no additional documents or testing for that exchange.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A CP holder must be at least eighteen to exchange the permit.
cards.back: A CP holder must be at least eighteen to exchange the permit for Class C, surrender the permit or affirm inability to surrender it, and pass the road driving test.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The CP-to-Class-C applicant must sign an affidavit documenting.
cards.back: The CP-to-Class-C applicant must sign an affidavit documenting forty hours of supervised driving, including six nighttime hours.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: An unlicensed applicant aged at least eighteen may apply directly for Class.
cards.back: An unlicensed applicant aged at least eighteen may apply directly for Class C by meeting document requirements, passing the knowledge and road examinations, and attesting to forty supervised driving hours including six at night.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: An adult who wants supervised practice before full.
cards.back: An adult who wants supervised practice before full licensing may instead obtain a Class C instructional permit.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A new Georgia resident who wants to drive must apply for the.
cards.back: A new Georgia resident who wants to drive must apply for the Georgia license or permit within thirty days of establishing residency, subject to the handbook's stated exceptions.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A new resident without a valid out-of-state permit or license.
cards.back: A new resident without a valid out-of-state permit or license follows Georgia's first-issuance process, with the appropriate teen or adult requirements.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A transfer applicant younger than eighteen with a valid license or permit.
cards.back: A transfer applicant younger than eighteen with a valid license or permit from another state or the District of Columbia normally qualifies for a comparable Georgia document only after meeting Georgia school, driver-education and awareness-program conditions.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: For the adult state-to-state transfer route, the earlier license must be.
cards.back: For the adult state-to-state transfer route, the earlier license must be surrendered and must not have been expired for two years or more.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: If an adult transfer applicant cannot surrender the earlier valid license, the.
cards.back: If an adult transfer applicant cannot surrender the earlier valid license, the handbook requires a certified driving history from the issuing state, dated within thirty days and showing valid status.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The regular transfer minimum is age eighteen. A seventeen-year-old may transfer an.
cards.back: The regular transfer minimum is age eighteen. A seventeen-year-old may transfer an equivalent valid Class C license only when it has no restrictions on time, route, driving purpose or passengers.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: An adult transfer applicant must provide the full Social Security number for.
cards.back: An adult transfer applicant must provide the full Social Security number for verification, identity and citizenship or lawful-presence evidence, two Georgia residence documents, and pass a vision screening.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Transfer identity and lawful-presence documents must be originals.
cards.back: Transfer identity and lawful-presence documents must be originals or certified copies; a fax is not acceptable.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: For a foreign credential missing from the applicant's possession, the handbook calls.
cards.back: For a foreign credential missing from the applicant's possession, the handbook calls for an English-language driving history from the issuing country dated within the last thirty days.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Most noncitizens may keep a valid foreign driving or identification document after.
cards.back: Most noncitizens may keep a valid foreign driving or identification document after Georgia issues its equivalent. A United States citizen must surrender foreign-issued driving and identification credentials.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: A document issued outside the United States states and the District of.
cards.back: A document issued outside the United States states and the District of Columbia is generally processed as a new Georgia issuance, including the examinations applicable to the requested class and required identity, lawful-presence, Social Security and residence evidence.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Foreign-country applicants ordinarily complete knowledge, road and vision examinations; some countries have.
cards.back: Foreign-country applicants ordinarily complete knowledge, road and vision examinations; some countries have testing exemptions listed by DDS. The handbook does not identify those countries on this page.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: Applicants younger than eighteen transferring from outside the.
cards.back: Applicants younger than eighteen transferring from outside the country must also satisfy the additional teen-licensing requirements.

cards.front: Complete the statement beginning: The handbook warns that privately operated sites may charge for information or.
cards.back: The handbook warns that privately operated sites may charge for information or training. It identifies the DDS government website as the official Georgia licensing source.
